subject.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands

question: Should cancellation preserve an already-started Gmail send as a successful partial result while force-killing unresponsive read-only child processes after 250 ms?
rationale: Tests establish the implementation behavior, but they cannot decide whether partial delivery should use an `ok` envelope or whether 250 ms is the intended permanent cleanup allowance for supported external commands.

options.title: Accept the bounded contract
options.body: Merge the current behavior: finish an already-started send, stop later drafts, and force-kill unresponsive read-only children after 250 ms.

options.title: Revise the result contract
options.body: Require a distinguishable partial-cancellation outcome or different grace policy before merging.

options.title: Limit cancellation scope
options.body: Land cancellation only for read-only subprocesses and defer Gmail send batching semantics to separate work.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Merge the current behavior: finish an already-started send, stop later drafts, and force-kill unresponsive read-only children after 250 ms.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent timeout and runtime-execution history makes steipete the strongest available owner for this cross-command cancellation contract.
